intro: Covers the US session of Monday 9 November (closed around 08:00 Sydney). This is the 08:15 retry: the SPI 200 readings are undated and differ between sources, and the prior ASX 200 close could not be reconciled, so futures are shown as a range and the implied open in points is not available.
footnotes: Index closes and VIX from Yahoo Finance (VIX page header shows 20.04, -21.83%). Yield, AUD/USD, Brent, gold and iron ore are Trading Economics CFD-based reference prices; Yahoo shows the 10-year at 4.864% and gold futures at US$4,147.40/oz; Trading Economics text gives Brent at US$92.76 and AUD/USD at 0.6928. Iron ore is essentially flat and may be a stale print.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures (December contract) are indicated higher, roughly +0.6% to +1.0% (about 9,118 to 9,135.5; midpoint about +0.8%). The two readings (TradingView +0.63%, Investing.com +0.96%) are undated and may predate the US rally, so treat the figure as approximate. That implies an ASX 200 open roughly 0.6-1.0% higher. An implied open in points is not available because Monday's ASX 200 close could not be reconciled (sources show 9,100.9, +0.10%, and about 9,030, +0.2%).

local_events: Westpac consumer sentiment (November, around 10:30 AEDT, consensus 78.3)
NAB business survey (October, around 11:30 AEDT, prior confidence -13, consensus -14)
Times are approximate. Notable local earnings: not available.
what_moved: Wall Street rallied sharply as Brent fell about 5.6% on reports that further US strikes on Iran are "highly unlikely" if talks progress, easing inflation worries, and as buyers returned after last week's tech/AI selloff (the Nasdaq fell about 5.5% on 5 November). Strong October payrolls (about 165k vs about 65k expected) kept a December Fed hike priced at roughly 80% but did not stop the rally. S&P 500 sector moves: not available; among large caps Caterpillar, Tesla, Meta and Goldman Sachs gained while Nvidia fell about 4%.

news.headline: Oil slumps on Iran hopes.
news.summary: Brent fell about 5.6% to US$92.80/bbl after reports that the US sees further strikes on Iran as unlikely if talks progress, though other reports cited a tanker hit near Hormuz and a US strike on Qeshm Island.

news.headline: Strong US jobs, Fed hike odds high.
news.summary: October payrolls rose about 165k against about 65k forecast with unemployment at 4.1%; markets price about an 80% chance of a 25bp Fed hike in December (fed funds 4.00%).

news.headline: Tech rebounds after selloff.
news.summary: The Nasdaq Composite gained 2.74% after last week's AI-led slide, though Nvidia fell about 4% amid headlines about a probe of its CEO and ongoing debate over AI investment payoffs.

news.headline: RBA lifts cash rate to 4.85%.
news.summary: The RBA raised rates for a fifth time this year in a 6-3 vote and dropped its tightening bias; swaps imply about 80% odds rates have peaked.

news.headline: US midterms shift Congress.
news.summary: Democrats won control of both chambers, and markets are weighing the prospect of tighter AI regulation.

news.headline: China's central bank adds gold.
news.summary: The PBoC bought 25.8 t in October, its largest monthly addition in three years, according to World Gold Council data.

coming_up: US October CPI is due Tuesday 10 November at 8:30am ET (00:30 AEDT Wednesday 11 November); consensus is +0.2% m/m and 3.8% y/y headline, core 2.7% y/y. RBA Assistant Governor Baker speaks around 10:30 AEDT Thursday 12 November; US PPI follows Friday 13 November.
